claims.summary: The exported greatest-common-divisor function returns the unsigned greatest common divisor of its two 32-bit inputs, represented as a 32-bit value.
claims.statement:
∀ (a b : BitVec 32),
  FVA.Wasm.Exec.Returns Examples.Rust.Lifted.module "gcd" [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 a, FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 b]
    [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 (BitVec.ofNat 32 (a.toNat.gcd b.toNat))]
claims.reason: For every pair of 32-bit inputs, the result is their unsigned greatest common divisor; the examples, including gcd(0, 0) = 0, agree with the intent.
claims.name: Examples.Rust.gcd
claims.intent: `gcd(a, b)` on unsigned 32-bit ints: their greatest common divisor (`gcd(a, 0) = a`).
details: Inputs: two 32-bit bit patterns, interpreted as unsigned integers for the greatest-common-divisor calculation; the result is reduced modulo 2 to the 32nd power.
The claim covers every pair of inputs. Returns additionally guarantees the module can be instantiated and that every call terminates without trapping, under every host behavior.

claims.summary: The exported clamp function returns the lower bound when the value is below it, the upper bound when the value is above it, and otherwise returns the value, using signed comparisons.
claims.statement:
∀ (x lo hi : BitVec 32),
  FVA.Wasm.Exec.Returns Examples.Rust.Lifted.module "clamp"
    [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 x, FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 lo, FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 hi]
    [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 (if x.slt lo = true then lo else if hi.slt x = true then hi else x)]
claims.reason: The signed comparisons select the lower bound when x is below it, the upper bound when x is above it, and x otherwise. When bounds are reversed, the lower-bound check takes priority, as in clamp(1, 3, 2) → 3.
claims.name: Examples.Rust.clamp
claims.intent: `clamp(x, lo, hi)` on signed 32-bit ints: `lo` below `lo`, `hi` above `hi`, else `x`.
details: Inputs: three 32-bit bit patterns: the value, lower bound, and upper bound. Comparisons interpret them as signed 32-bit integers; the returned value is whichever input bit pattern the comparisons select.
The claim covers every triple of inputs. Returns additionally guarantees the module can be instantiated and that every call terminates without trapping, under every host behavior.
caveats: The comparison is signed, but the inputs and selected result are still 32-bit bit patterns; the claim does not require the lower bound to be less than or equal to the upper bound.
